How much does the growth model change the projection?

Projected change in annual growth of the archive's trees at their current size, 2071–2100 versus 1985–2014 under SSP5-8.5, from five models that describe past growth about equally well. Switch the model and watch the map.

The models

T+S embeds a Richards-type size-dependent growth potential and Liebig-type, monotone limitation by temperature and moisture as hard constraints; a neural network predicts their site-specific parameters. U+S is an unconstrained network of equal capacity with the same inputs. XGB, tuned gradient-boosted trees. LMM, linear mixed-effects model. T+S acc, an exploratory version with site-specific adjustment of the moisture thresholds.

Read with care

Values describe trees of the tree-ring archive at fixed current size, not forest productivity or the carbon sink. Projections include neither CO₂ fertilization nor competition. Site values are the mean over sampled trees and five climate models (GFDL-ESM4, IPSL-CM6A-LR, MPI-ESM1-2-HR, MRI-ESM2-0, UKESM1-0-LL); the map shows the 3,772 sites with projected trees, sensitivities are given for 6,263 sites.

Source

Ercanlı, İ. Growth theory changes projected tree-growth responses to climate despite similar historical skill (manuscript under review). Data: International Tree-Ring Data Bank (NOAA WDS-Paleo), CRU TS 4.09, CMIP6. Code and outputs: github.com/ilkerercanli/growth-theory-ai.
